title: Feature Engineering Laboratory
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Build new features from five raw housing columns with a product, ratio, sum, difference, square, or log, preview each one, and see the real change in cross-validated R squared when it joins a linear regression model.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to construct new features from existing columns and use cross-validated R squared to decide which of them improve a linear regression model.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Open-ended construction with an immediate preview and a validation score
keyQuestions: Why does a linear model gain nothing from A + B when A and B are already features?
Why does taking the log of a right-skewed column often help a linear model?
Why is CV R², and not Train R², the number that decides whether a feature stays?
commonMisconceptions: Any new feature improves the model (Train R² always rises a little, but CV R² falls when the feature carries no new information).
A feature with a low correlation with the target is useless (a squared term can have almost no correlation with price and still let the model fit a curve).
Adding the sum of two columns gives the model new information (the model could already form any weighted sum of its features).
Each feature has a fixed importance (what a feature is worth depends on which other features are in the model).
assessmentOpportunities: Students propose one engineered feature for a new data set, justify it from domain knowledge, and state which number they would check to decide whether to keep it and why Train R² is not that number.
